title: Go behind the badge: Rowlett's Citizen's Police Academy is taking applications
excerpt: Eight Thursday evenings, a morning at the gun range and an inside look at how Rowlett police keep the city safe. Only 15 spots.
body:
Ever wondered what really happens behind the scenes at the Rowlett Police Department? Here's your chance to find out.

The department is now taking applications for Citizen's Police Academy Class #48. That number says a lot: Rowlett police have opened their doors to residents this way for 47 classes before this one.

Over eight Thursday evenings, participants get an inside look at how officers investigate crimes, respond to emergencies and serve the community. The schedule includes:

- A station tour, including dispatch and the jail
- Crime scene investigation
- Patrol, arrest tactics and DWI enforcement
- The SWAT, traffic and Problem Solving units
- Dog Walker Watch and what to do in an active shooter situation
- A Saturday morning session at the gun range

The details:

- When: Thursdays, January 14 – March 4, 2027, 6 – 8 p.m., plus Saturday, March 6, 8 – 11 a.m.
- Where: Rowlett Police Department
- Who: Anyone 18 or older who lives or works in Rowlett

Class size is limited to 15 people, chosen first-come, first-served, so don't wait.

Whether you're thinking about a career in law enforcement, want to get more involved in your community, or are just curious, this is a great way to meet the people behind the badge.

Apply at bit.ly/4fFB3GH. Questions? Contact Officer Erick Mitchell, Neighborhood Services, at emitchell@rowlett.com or 972-412-6242 (Tuesday – Friday).
